mechanism_narrative: Persistent week-over-week declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate a continuing contraction in commuting and discretionary travel; this suppresses weekday and weekend retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than over the last 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continuing to decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the PARKS series falls below -40 percent, outdoor recreation activity has collapsed sufficiently to remove a major complementary trip generator for retail areas; RETAIL_REC therefore declines further over the next 14 days.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -40 percent in a weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is equal to or higher than over the last 14 days after PARKS falls below -40 percent.

mechanism_narrative: A joint regime of elevated RESIDENTIAL above +15 percent and depressed WORKPLACES below -40 percent signals widespread stay-at-home behavior; this directly reduces retail-and-recreation visits, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next 28 days.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than over the last 28 days when RESIDENTIAL is above +15 and WORKPLACES is below -40.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime where TRANSIT is below -40 percent and GROCERY_PHARM turns negative, even essential-trip mobility is contracting; consumers cut non-essential retail trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next 7 days.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is equal to or higher than over the last 7 days when TRANSIT is below -40 and GROCERY_PHARM is negative.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is equal to or higher than over the last 7 days despite the prior four-week decline in RETAIL_REC.
